subject: general
question: What was the main occupation of the majority of the Indian population during the period immediately after independence (around 1947)?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Agriculture**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Agriculture was the primary occupation of the Indian population immediately after independence, with the majority of the workforce engaged in farming-related activities.
 
• India's economy was predominantly agrarian during the 1947 period, with over 70% of the population relying on agriculture for their livelihood.
 
• The agricultural sector contributed significantly to the GDP of India, as industries and services were underdeveloped at the time.
 
• Most farmers practiced subsistence farming, growing food crops like rice, wheat, and millet to meet their own needs rather than for commercial purposes.
 
• The Indian government introduced land reforms and policies post-independence to improve agricultural productivity and address rural poverty.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Subsistence Farming:** A type of farming in which farmers grow crops primarily for their own consumption rather than for sale or trade.
 
• **Land Reforms:** After independence, the Indian government implemented measures like the abolition of the Zamindari system and redistribution of land to promote equitable land ownership.
 
• **Green Revolution:** Initiated in the 1960s, it significantly boosted agricultural production through the use of high-yield crop varieties, fertilizers, and irrigation techniques.
 
• **Challenges in Agriculture:** Post-independence, Indian agriculture faced issues such as outdated farming techniques, low productivity, and dependence on monsoons for irrigation.
 
• **Rural Economy:** The agricultural sector was the backbone of India's rural economy, with the majority of villages relying on farming and related activities for their sustenance.
